item.title: Module 1: Red Team Methodology
item.description: The seven-phase red team methodology: preparation, intelligence, reconnaissance, access, post exploitation, cleanup and backout, and reporting, with the judgment behind each.

item.title: Module 2: Mission Preparation and Infrastructure
item.description: Everything required before an attack: scope and rules of engagement, deconfliction, hardening the attack platform, standing up redirectors, and validating the infrastructure before go.

item.description: Master networking for the CompTIA A+ 220-1201 Core 1 exam. Learn TCP and UDP ports, wireless technologies, networked host services, network hardware, SOHO configuration, and tools.

item.title: Module 3: Networking and Active Directory Foundations
item.description: The networking and Active Directory concepts every red team technique builds on: HTTP and HTTPS, TCP and UDP, the domain controller, users, groups, and group nesting.

item.description: Separate profile validity, working communication, telemetry, and detection with a local HTTP exercise and controlled comparison record.

item.title: Module 8: Open-Source Intelligence
item.description: Evaluate public sources, RDAP, DNS, certificate logs, and scan data. Build a traceable OSINT brief with worked examples and source-quality checks.

item.title: Module 9: Active Reconnaissance and Scanning
item.description: Interpret Nmap port states, scan methods, and vantage points through a loopback exercise, segmentation case, and evidence-based scan plan.

item.title: CompTIA A+ (220-1202): Operational Procedures
item.category: "CompTIA A+ Course" , "Operational Procedures" , "Documentation" , "Change Management" , "Backups" , "IT Support" , "CompTIA Certification" , "Help Desk" , "Professionalism" , "IT Fundamentals"
item.description: Master operational procedures for the CompTIA A+ 220-1202 Core 2 exam. Learn documentation, change management, backups, safety, environmental controls, communication, scripting, and AI basics.

item.title: Module 10: Initial Access: Phishing and Delivery
item.description: Distinguish phishing delivery, interaction, execution, and access. Interpret campaign metrics, modern Office controls, and Windows architecture with worked examples.

item.title: Module 11: Situational Awareness and Host Operations
item.description: Build a current host-state record using Windows and Linux identity, process, socket, and routing evidence, with a worked snapshot comparison.

item.title: Module 12: User Persistence
item.description: Understand user startup triggers, HKCU context, and restoration. Follow a benign Notepad Run-entry lab with evidence and cleanup checks.

item.title: Module 13: Local Privilege Escalation
item.description: Evaluate Windows privilege escalation paths through service permissions, DLL loading, evidence quality, and a read-only lab exercise.

item.title: Module 14: Privileged Persistence and Process Migration
item.description: Understand Windows service persistence, process lifetime, architecture, and migration tradeoffs through read-only inspection and a service lifecycle exercise.

item.title: Module 15: Persistence Cleanup and Defense Evasion
item.description: Restore persistence changes with a precise artifact ledger, correct registry identity, evidence preservation, and independent verification of cleanup.

item.title: Module 16: Domain Privilege Escalation and Kerberos Abuse
item.description: Analyze Kerberos service-ticket exposure, account privilege, encryption choices, and delegation evidence with a domain escalation review record.
